record.paper_title: Imaging with LINC-NIRVANA, the Fizeau interferometer of the Large Binocular Telescope: state of the art and open problems
record.original_question: How can blind or myopic deconvolution for LINC-NIRVANA be made mathematically sound and computationally efficient when the point-spread functions are unknown or only partly known? The formulation should jointly estimate the astronomical object and the point-spread functions under physical constraints such as nonnegativity, band-limiting, and known Strehl-ratio information, and should exploit the relationship between this deconvolution problem and nonnegative matrix factorization to obtain convergence analysis and practical reconstruction algorithms.

evidence.quote: blind deconvolution is an interesting and basic problem

artifact.category_tag: Blind deconvolution and nonnegative matrix factorization
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a multi-frame imaging model in which p observed images g_j : Z^2 -> R_{>=0} (j = 1, ..., p) of a common astronomical object f : Z^2 -> R_{>=0} are produced by convolution with unknown point-spread functions (PSFs) K_j : Z^2 -> R_{>=0}, possibly corrupted by Poisson noise:

   g_j ≈ Poisson(K_j * f),   j = 1, ..., p.

The object f and each PSF K_j are required to satisfy the following physical constraints:
  (i) Nonnegativity: f >= 0, K_j >= 0.
  (ii) Normalization / flux conservation: sum_x K_j(x) = 1.
  (iii) Band-limiting: the Fourier transforms of the K_j are supported in a prescribed bounded region Ω ⊂ R^2 (the optical transfer function support of a Fizeau interferometric aperture).
  (iv) Strehl-ratio information: a known lower bound s_j ∈ (0,1] on the Strehl ratio of K_j, defined as the ratio of the peak of the in-focus PSF to that of the corresponding diffraction-limited PSF.

The joint blind (or myopic, when partial knowledge of K_j is available) deconvolution problem is to recover (f, K_1, ..., K_p) from the data {g_j} by minimizing a data-fidelity functional (e.g. the Kullback–Leibler divergence)

   J(f, K_1, ..., K_p) = sum_{j=1}^p D_{KL}(g_j || K_j * f)

subject to constraints (i)–(iv).

Tasks:

(a) Reformulate this constrained joint estimation problem as a nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) problem, identifying the matrices whose nonnegative factorization corresponds to (f, K_1, ..., K_p) and showing how the constraints (i)–(iv) translate into constraints on the factors.

(b) Using this reformulation, design a computationally efficient iterative algorithm (for example, of multiplicative-update or alternating-projection type) that enforces all constraints (i)–(iv) at every iteration.

(c) Provide a rigorous convergence analysis: prove that the iterates produce a monotonically nonincreasing sequence of objective values and that limit points are stationary points of J on the constraint set.

(d) Establish identifiability/uniqueness conditions (up to natural ambiguities) under which the joint reconstruction of f and the K_j is well-posed given the constraints (i)–(iv).
artifact.status_search_result: Blind and myopic deconvolution under nonnegativity, band-limit and Strehl-ratio constraints, and its connection with nonnegative matrix factorization, has been investigated (e.g. by Bertero, Boccacci and collaborators) with partial algorithmic results, but no fully satisfactory algorithm combining mathematical soundness, computational efficiency and complete convergence/identifiability analysis under all listed physical constraints has been established. The problem remains generally regarded as open.

status_evidence.title: Nonnegative matrix factorization and blind deconvolution: review
status_evidence.snippet: Blind deconvolution problems can be reformulated as constrained nonnegative matrix factorization, but convergence and uniqueness under physical constraints remain only partially understood.
status_evidence.claim: The reformulation as NMF is known, and partial convergence results exist, but full theory is lacking.

status_evidence.title: Bertero–Boccacci, blind deconvolution in astronomical imaging
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses blind/myopic deconvolution for interferometric imaging and lists open mathematical issues regarding convergence and constraint handling.
status_evidence.claim: Authors explicitly describe the problem as open and basic.
